note: Round-3 roadmap: every round-2 item not FULLY_ADDRESSED, graded at its round-2 residual obligation class (C1 and C3 declined by the author and dropped), plus the three round-2 new issues (NEW-1 previously missed, NEW-2 and NEW-3 regressions), all treated as should_fix by the author's choice.

items.text: Survey published multidimensional-BC metric comparisons (how eps set, coverage reported) or reframe as a pre-emptive guideline; drop 'A common way'
items.round2_residual_gap: No survey (option a) and no explicit statement that the note is a pre-emptive guideline (option b); the new claim that these choices 'rarely' reach methods sections (abstract, §1) is itself an unsupported prevalence claim, and 'which is how most BC studies start' (§3) remains uncited. Either support/cite these or remove them and state the guideline framing explicitly.
items.round2_criterion: Either (a) a stated, reproducible literature survey (search terms/databases/date, inclusion rule) of published multidimensional bounded-confidence studies that compare distance metrics, tabulating per study how epsilon was set per metric and whether realised or initial coverage was reported, and the prevalence wording in abstract/intro/sec.3 matches what the survey found; or (b) the paper is explicitly reframed as a pre-emptive guideline, with prevalence language removed. In both cases the phrase 'A common way' (or any equivalent unsupported prevalence claim, incl. 'conventional bounds' used as prevalence) no longer appears unsupported.

items.text: Recast section 5 on a documented, citable, archived model; short disclosure of the draft + policy stakes
items.round2_residual_gap: The case model is not yet citable/archived (DOI placeholder printed in the text and bibliography); PolicySwarm has no documented specification beyond a prose paragraph and the perception formula (no ODD or update equations, unlike the minimal model); the backward experiment runs 'the draft's own engine', but the revised Code and data statement removed the identifier (commit 50a42e5 and patch) that the original gave for it, so that engine is now uninspectable.
items.round2_criterion: Section 5 rests on a model a reader can inspect: a documented specification (ODD or equations) plus a citable, archived version (persistent identifier/DOI or archived commit) of the case model; the case is presented as a demonstration of how each protocol item catches its artefact rather than as correction of an inaccessible draft; draft history reduced to a short disclosure stating it is the author's own, unreleased work caught before external use; and 2-3 sentences stating the policy reading the withdrawn result would have supported.

items.text: Run-matching as an estimand; report t=0 and run-matched side by side; add one outcome-independent calibration; state mechanically tied outcomes; remove 'removes the gap'
items.round2_residual_gap: No outcome-independent calibration (e.g. early-window interactions per agent) is run or reported, which the criterion requires; the response curves are a sweep against realised pass rate, not an outcome-independent match. Side-by-side reporting is incomplete for variance/dispersion (given only under run-matching in §4.2). §5 labels the run-matched design 'recommended' without saying why that estimand is preferred there.
items.round2_criterion: Run-matching is defined as an estimand ('geometry effect at equal realised interaction rate') distinct from t=0 matching ('effect including the interaction-rate channel'); results under t=0 and run-matched calibration are reported side by side for the minimal model outcomes; at least one outcome-independent calibration (e.g. transient/early-window interactions per agent, first ~50-100 rounds) is run and its results reported; the text states which outcomes are mechanically tied to the realised pass rate (group count/structure) and why; and the claims that run-matching 'removes the gap'/'removes geometry effects' (abstract, sec.4.4, protocol item 3) are dropped or replaced by estimand-qualified wording.

items.text: Related-work section (R2's verified references first; model alignment/docking; BC surveys); cite or drop flache2017
items.round2_residual_gap: No related-work section positioning the paper; R2's verified missing references are uncited and will not appear in the bibliography; flache2017 still uncited; the previously correct grimm2020 ODD citation was dropped (made-worse trigger, peripheral) and should be restored in Appendix A.
items.round2_criterion: A dedicated related-work section (or equivalent integrated subsection) citing R2's verified missing references first (e.g. Lorenz 2007 survey, Fortunato et al. 2005, Huet/Deffuant/Jager 2008, Kurahashi-Nakamura et al. 2016, Baumann et al. 2021, Aggarwal et al. 2001), the model alignment/docking tradition, and BC surveys, each tied to how this paper relates to it; flache2017 either cited in text or removed from refs.bib.

items.text: Position as static volume matching (Lorenz) -> distribution coverage -> dynamic matching; say which protocol items are new
items.round2_residual_gap: Identify which of the six audit-list items are new contributions and which restate existing practice (e.g. item 5 restates Gelman and Stern; item 4 is a known identity).

items.text: Report unconverged share per cell; correct the 'exceptions' sentence (l.161); report convergence time
items.round2_residual_gap: Report the unsettled share per cell and per metric (not only pooled Euclidean), define 'still changing/settled', and report convergence time; 26% of Euclidean runs are unsettled at the 2,000-round primary horizon and 13% at 4,000, so the claim that the group gap 'is not a transient here' needs per-cell support.

items.text: Report achieved calibration error per cell with CIs; flag out-of-tolerance cells; max_iter/monotonicity check; pilot-size guidance
items.round2_residual_gap: Achieved error is reported on pilot seeds only, without CIs; the two of 36 cases whose realised pass-rate gap is not equivalent on the evaluation seeds are not identified; several cells sit exactly at the tolerance (+/-0.005); max_iter is not stated; protocol item 3 gives no pilot-size guidance relative to between-seed SD.

items.text: Per-cell paired bootstrap CIs; pre-stated equivalence margins (TOST) for 'removes'/'behave as one'; report cosine and angular separately
items.round2_residual_gap: Per-cell gaps with CIs are referred to 'result tables' that are not in the manuscript; margins (+/-0.02, +/-0.25) are not justified; cosine and angular, which the paper shows are one gate, are pooled in all 36-case medians and counts (double-weighting near-duplicates); 'one gate' and 'one common ruler removes the difference' are asserted from point maxima, not TOST (and the own-ruler median 0.12 is itself inside the paper's 0.25 margin); new case-study null claims ('lag has no effect' from 100 [97,103]; 'disappears' / 'whether the geometries differ at all' from +0.001 [-0.004,+0.007], while the two indices are 134 [129,139] vs 150 [145,154]) rest on non-significance, contrary to the paper's own audit item 5.
items.round2_criterion: Per-cell paired-bootstrap 95% CIs on the reported gaps (Fig.2 and text); equivalence margins stated (with justification, ahead of the equivalence results) and TOST used for every 'removes'/'behave as one'-type claim, with those claims kept only where equivalence is shown; cosine and angular reported separately (or only one, without pooling near-duplicates); the 'almost every gap differs significantly ... so we report sizes' sentence corrected for run-matching.

items.text: Short discussion: protocol cost; which published results to revisit

Interaction estimand undefined and not reconciled with the lag index. The paper's main case claim rests on 'Euclidean's lag contrast in the relative shock effect minus cosine's', but 'relative shock effect' is never defined, and the interaction and the index disagree in ordering in some cells without comment: centred/run/anchor/own-opinion gives indices Euclidean 134 [129,139] < cosine 150 [145,154] (by the index, cosine amplifies more) yet interaction +0.001 [-0.004,+0.007]; unit/run/anchor/centre gives 189 vs 187 yet interaction +0.020 [+0.014,+0.027]. Readers cannot tell which estimand carries 'which geometry amplified the lag effect more'.

Fig. 4 row labels and caption do not map consistently onto the text. Caption says the fixes (cos, rng, split) are 'applied (1) or not (0)', but rows are labelled split=30/40. Measured from the figure, the text's 'draft's own engine and settings' interaction (+0.034 [+0.025,+0.044]) matches the cos=0 rng=0 split=30 row (~+0.034 [+0.024,+0.044]) and the 'all other fixes' value (+0.029 [+0.020,+0.039]) matches cos=1 rng=1 split=40, while the trust-only variant of the draft (+0.026 [+0.013,+0.038]) sits on cos=0 rng=0 split=40 and the all-fixes+trust row on split=30. No single reading of 'split' makes all four consistent.

The response-curve experiment that the abstract offers as the paper's answer ('we report whole response curves instead') is undocumented: the threshold grid, seeds (50, apparently separate from the factorial's 100), horizon and how the realised pass rate is computed appear nowhere in §4.1 or the ODD, and the curves carry no uncertainty bands.
